title: とても — “very”
summary: とても is an adverb meaning ‘very’. It goes before an adjective (or a verb that shows feeling or degree) and raises the degree. It is the most common and neutral word for ‘very’ in everyday Japanese.

patterns.gloss: とても + adjective (とても寒い, とてもきれいだ)

body.p: Put とても directly before the word it strengthens: とても寒いです, とてもおいしいです. It does not change the adjective's form. It works with both い- and な-adjectives.
In a positive sentence とても means ‘very’. With a negative, it does not mean ‘not very’; use あまり～ない for that. A negative with とても is usually avoided at this level.
There are casual or stronger words: すごく, 本当に, ちょっと (a little). In formal writing you may see 大変 or 非常に.

examples.ja: この料理（りょうり）はとてもおいしいです。
examples.romaji: Kono ryōri wa totemo oishii desu.

examples.ja: 今日（きょう）はとても寒（さむ）いです。
examples.note: とても goes right before 寒い.

examples.ja: この犬（いぬ）はとてもかわいいです。
examples.romaji: Kono inu wa totemo kawaii desu.
examples.note: Works the same with any adjective.

pitfalls: Don't change the adjective: とても寒いです, not とても寒くです.
For ‘not very’, use あまり～ない, not とても with a negative.
